text:
Team, a recent deploy caused a checkout outage. The migration ran an ALTER TABLE that added a new NOT NULL column with a default value. That statement locked the table for 6 minutes, and 2,300 checkout requests failed while it held the lock. Each of those was a customer trying to buy something, and we're sorry.

We're changing how we ship schema changes. Every schema change will now be reviewed for lock impact before it goes out. We're also switching to an expand-and-contract approach: add the column as nullable, backfill it in small batches, and enforce the constraint only after the data is in place. Finally, we're adding lock timeouts to our migration tooling, so a blocked statement fails quickly instead of stalling production.

Checkout is the part of the product we can least afford to break. Thanks for your patience while we put these changes in place.
